what: The dispatcher reserves host scratch disk per job the same way it reserves memory. Each tick reads the scratch root's free space once with statfs (ULPIN_DOCUMENT_OCR_SCRATCH when set, else os.tmpdir()) and subtracts a 2048 MiB floor; a job starts only when its lane has room, its memory fits and its scratch fits what is unreserved. A job that writes no scratch is never refused for scratch; a job whose scratch is larger than the whole budget starts only when no held job writes scratch. A job refused for scratch is recorded with its first refusal and holds back newer non-probe jobs after DISPATCH_HEAD_OF_LINE_MS, as for memory. A failed statfs logs one line with the error code only and leaves scratch unlimited for that tick. The tick's SQL, the lanes' concurrency and memory admission are unchanged.
budget: floor(bavail * bsize / MiB) - DISPATCH_SCRATCH_FLOOR_MIB (2048) of the scratch root, read once a tick; Infinity when the read fails

table.source: TABULAR_STREAM_LIMITS.bytes (7 GiB), the largest workbook read as a stream, copied whole into scratch by tabular-stream.ts scratchFolder, which requires its size and 1 GiB more free (XW1)

probe, vector, document, raster, point,.source: no job in these lanes writes under the scratch root, except the operations with their own rule below

operationScratch.operation: any processor operation (processor: true) and any operation no row names
operationScratch.source: runs in the processor's container, not on this host's scratch root

operationScratch.scratchMiB: 0 for a CSV selection (read in place); otherwise the table lane default 8192, because the payload (TableProfileInputSchema) names no source size
ceil(payload.sourceBytes / MiB) + 1024 for a tabular read of a workbook; 0 for a CSV or GIS read; 8192 for a workbook without a size
operationScratch.source: AnyStreamingInputSchema: tabular.selection.format and sourceBytes; streaming-vector-worker.ts reads windows through readTableWindows
reads stored windows, never a file; stated so the table lane default does not apply
document-ocr.ts privateOcrDirectory under ULPIN_DOCUMENT_OCR_SCRATCH: the PDF copy, at most DOCUMENT_LIMITS.originalBytes 16 MiB, plus the 128 KiB result and 64 KiB receipt limits

gaps: table-profile: its payload names no workbook size, so every workbook read reserves the 8192 MiB lane default. Adding the source's bytes to TableProfileInputSchema (packages/server/src/modules/usp/ingestion/table-profile-worker.ts, not owned here) would let it reserve its size plus 1024 MiB.

document-extraction: the OCR worker's own page renders and temporary files (scripts/usp/document-models/run_source_ocr.py, which also receives TEMP) are not measured; only the PDF copy and the result and receipt limits are counted.

Native readers that copy their original into their own profile's scratchRoot are not counted, because that root is configured separately and this budget does not read it: ifc-native, dxf-native, kml-native, citygml-native, obj-native, gltf-native, geoparquet-native (each *-processor.ts mkdtemp under config.scratchRoot) and cityjson-validation (ULPIN_CITYJSON_VALIDATOR_SCRATCH_ROOT). They reserve 0 here.

packet-pdf may reach the packet region runtime (region-runtime.ts, ULPIN_PACKET_REGIONS_SCRATCH), a separate root; it reserves 0 here. Document page and image previews (ULPIN_DOCUMENT_PAGES_SCRATCH, ULPIN_DOCUMENT_IMAGES_SCRATCH) run outside the dispatcher.

Free space is read each tick while held jobs are already writing, so bytes a running job has written are counted twice (in the lower free space and in its reservation) until it is released. This is conservative: it can delay a job, never overfill the disk.
Each dispatcher process reserves scratch for its own in-process jobs only, as it does memory; two dispatcher processes on one host do not see each other's scratch reservations.

cases: a workbook read reserves its copy and 1 GiB; a CSV, a GIS read and a stored-window job reserve none
every operation the processor runs, and any it is sent unnamed, reserves no scratch
two workbooks over the scratch budget start one after the other (a release lets the waiting one start)
a workbook over the whole scratch budget runs alone among the jobs that write scratch
a workbook refused for scratch stops newer jobs after the head-of-line wait, then starts when it fits
the scratch budget is the root's free space less the floor, read from the OCR scratch or the temp folder (fake statfs)
a scratch root that cannot be read logs one line and blocks nothing that tick (fake statfs failure)
